title: Assessment of the ten synthetic clinical systems (Table II) and their principle scores

method.assessment: Each of the ten built-in scenarios (backend/src/safeguard_pq/data/scenarios.json) is assessed once with seed 2026, the default options (independent planner, y = 5, z = 10, L = 10) and no LLM.
method.M: Mosca's test: pq_posture.mosca.at_risk, i.e. x + y > z with x = data lifetime, y = 5, z = 10 years (reported whatever the key exchange).
method.P: Lifetime override: 1 if the critical long_lifetime_classical_crypto finding is raised (x >= L = 10 years and the key exchange is neither PQ nor hybrid), else 0.
method.plan, projected S: Selected actions of the shipped planner and the explainer's plan_projection, which removes only the findings of the selected actions.
method.reassessed S / status: optimizer.reassess.evaluate_plan_by_reassessment: the plan's catalogue mitigations are applied to the configuration by code and the pipeline is re-run with the same seed (as in E9, benchmarks/plan_reassessment.py, plan A).
method.principle scores: tippss_scores of the baseline assessment (the six IEEE/UL 2933-2024 principles, called pillars in the code).
method.not reproduced: The timing in the note of Table III (6.31 ms per E1 assessment) is machine-dependent and is not re-measured here.

The framework rated seven of the ten systems UNSAFE, two AT_RISK and one SAFE.
The legacy TLS 1.0 system reached the highest PQ risk score (89).
The hybrid imaging gateway was rated partially PQ because its certificates were still ECDSA.
Among the systems with classical key exchange, Mosca's test and the override disagree only for the health-record interface (x = 8 years), which therefore has a medium rather than a critical finding.
